Charter F4 is explicit and binding: gloss/lamination rinse-out treatments are included and treated as shine-focused masks, with the claims claim-gated and conservative. The charter's F4 boundary-case list names this exact product.

g0.placementConjunctNote: The directions state 'von den Wurzeln bis in die Spitzen' — explicit ROOT application, which contradicts P5's canonical 'Längen und Spitzen, Ansatz aussparen'. Under R8's mask delta this is a protocol deviation that fires the root/scalp application review trigger; it does not silently change R8 and does not create a scalp property. tailMarker.anomalyNote: The earliest tail-class ingredient is a COLOURANT at rank 7 — the only cohort product where the marker is neither a fragrance nor a preservative, and the only one where Parfum is the FINAL entry (rank 30). §3.1's literal anomaly conditions are not met (rank 7 > 3, and Cetearyl Alcohol @2 and Behentrimonium Chloride @4 precede it), so the marker is technically resolved. But a colourant pair at ranks 7–8 in a list whose fragrance sits at 30 is not a plausible ~1% proxy: cosmetic colourants are typically used far below 1%, and this ordering is more consistent with a house listing convention or a retailer transcription artefact than with descending weight. I therefore fire `tail_marker_anomaly` by reviewer judgment and cap every affected field at moderate confidence, while still applying the marker as written. See AP-11-COLOURANT.  ||  TAIL MARKER RE-DERIVED UNDER v0.2 (R8 colourant precedence + R2 plausibility). v0.1 set tail_index = 7 on CI 17200/RED 33. Under Standard §3.1 and lexicon §0.2 as patched by R8, a colourant may no longer define the marker. Recomputing on the marker-eligible classes, the earliest is HYDROXYCITRONELLAL @12, a declared fragrance allergen named in §3.1's list. tail_index is therefore 12, not 7, and the credited segment grows from six entries to eleven, newly admitting CI 17200 @7 and CI 19140 @8 (recorded as E1 formula facts with zero care credit, exactly as Titanium Dioxide and Mica are - lexicon family 10), COCOS NUCIFERA OIL @9, SODIUM CHLORIDE @10 (family 10, zero credit) and HYDROXYPROPYL GUAR @11 (non-ionic thickener, zero care credit; also the tail_index - 1 species). PLAUSIBILITY ASSESSMENT (R2, §3.1.1): PLAUSIBLE - CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2, BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @4, AMODIMETHICONE @6 and COCOS NUCIFERA OIL @9 all outrank @12, and the product is a conventional O/W emulsion with AQUA/WATER @1. This closes v0.1's AP-11-COLOURANT, which fired `tail_marker_anomaly` by reviewer judgment: the anomaly is now resolved by rule rather than by judgment, and that trigger no longer fires. PARFUM/FRAGRANCE remains the final entry @30 - the house-convention pattern lexicon §0.2 warns about - and the allergen fallback is exactly what §0.2's marker-failure fallback prescribes.

The base here is a conventional cetearyl/behentrimonium/amodimethicone conditioning architecture with no protein route — which is exactly the pattern D6's own worked example describes, and it lands in `moisture`. E2 ceiling: comparative emphasis, not a delivered outcome.
evidenceSignals: no hydrolyzed protein, peptide, keratin, or cationised protein at ANY rank
CETEARYL ALCOHOL (2), BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (4), AMODIMETHICONE (6) — the conventional conditioning base D6 names for this product family
PROPYLENE GLYCOL (rank 5) — the only above-tail humectant
GLYCOLIC ACID (rank 29) — the hero acid, second from last in the list, contributing nothing to care_direction under D6
careDirection.derivation: §9.3 material-R5 test fails absolutely (no candidate species at any rank), closing `protein` and `balanced`. D6's gloss/lamination rule is applied verbatim: classify by the care base, not the acid claim. Residual = `moisture`.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `moisture`: a coherent conditioning architecture without a dominant protein-film route.
`protein` does not apply: no protein exists anywhere. (D6 notes the sibling case Balea Glow & Shine reaches `protein` because its keratin route is material; this product has no such route.)
`balanced` does not apply: its first conjunct is the material R5 route.
Confidence `moderate` rather than `high`: the route separation is unambiguous, but the fired `tail_marker_anomaly` and the aggregated source cap it.

Re-checked under v0.2 (R6, on the re-derived segment). `moisture` STANDS. Reading (a) is unavailable (no R5 species at any rank). Reading (b) — the film-/acid-led `neither_dominant` read whose named anchor case in §9.3 is THIS PRODUCT — is tested in full and FAILS at clause 4. Clause 1 holds (no protein anchor). Clause 2 holds (AMODIMETHICONE @6 is a substantive R2 silicone above the tail, and GLYCOLIC ACID @29 is the R6a acid whose positioning carries the product). Clause 3 holds (one humectant-class species, PROPYLENE GLYCOL @5, is not a pair; and COCOS NUCIFERA OIL @9 alone does not satisfy S3, so there is no lipid stack). Clause 4 FAILS: it requires every film/acid species establishing clause 2 to rank ABOVE every candidate leg species noted under clause 3, and AMODIMETHICONE @6 sits one rank BELOW PROPYLENE GLYCOL @5. The reading is therefore refused on a single rank. This is a direct answer to §18 open question 6 and is escalated with AP-11-COCONUT: the standard names this product as reading (b)'s anchor case, and on its real INCI the clause the standard added to keep the read honest is exactly what blocks it.
counterSignals: The acid identity is carried entirely by the `shine` focus, not by care_direction — D6's explicit instruction, applied.
limitations: Banned wording observed absolutely — see the shine record.

R6a applied: glycolic acid TEMPORARILY PLASTICIZES the fibre (a measured decrease in Young's modulus). It does not seal, coat, close the cuticle, laminate, or produce lasting change, and it contributes nothing to this field.

Re-checked under v0.2 (R2, R8): `low` STANDS on the re-derived segment. Both use wording that R6a and §9.5.4 place on an absolute banned list. They are quoted here strictly as claim context; no part of this record adopts sealing, lasting, or lamination language.

primaryFocus.evidenceScope: Formula-first §9.5.2 hierarchy over above-tail ranks 1–11 on the RE-DERIVED marker; §9.5.4 shine threshold tested and failed.
primaryFocus.rationale: CHANGED under v0.2 (R8 → §9.5.4 criterion 1). With the marker re-derived to HYDROXYCITRONELLAL @12, COCOS NUCIFERA OIL @9 is an R4b heavy lipid above the tail, and §9.5.4 criterion 1 requires an optical-emphasis architecture WITH a comparatively low lipid load and no R4b heavy lipid above the tail. That criterion now fails, and §9.5.1's hard rule forbids a claim from making up the difference. The step-6 smoothing route — which was the blind-lane value under v0.1 — stands on the amino silicone. E2 ceiling: comparative surface-control potential, never a lasting or sealing effect.
evidenceSignals: COCOS NUCIFERA OIL (rank 9) — R4b heavy lipid above the re-derived marker: §9.5.4 criterion 1's low-lipid-load condition FAILS
AMODIMETHICONE (rank 6) — an alignment-oriented amino-functional R2 silicone above the tail: a distinct silicone route materially beyond the ordinary mask base, which is what §9.5.2 step 6 requires
BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (4) + CETEARYL ALCOHOL (2) — the R1 base; COCAMIDOPROPYL BETAINE @3 is amphoteric and is not counted as a cationic conditioning agent
HYDROXYPROPYL GUAR (11) is non-ionic and POLYQUATERNIUM-37 (17) is in the tail — there is no R3 cationic-polymer route above the tail
GLYCOLIC ACID (rank 29, second from last) — R6a acid-gloss context: supporting context, never sufficient, and at that rank it earns nothing
claims: '19% Gloss-Complex mit Glykolsäure', 'erstes Haar-Laminierungs-Produkt von L'Oréal Paris für zuhause', 'für stumpfes, poröses Haar'; product name 'Glycolic Gloss, 5-Minuten Haar-Laminierung'
primaryFocus.derivation: Step 1 baseline exclusion applied. Step 2: one M1 base observation plus one M3 optical observation. Step 3: `repair` blocked (no R5, no bond token; R6a can never set repair); `curl_support` blocked (single cationic, no above-tail polymer); `color_care` blocked (the CI entries are the product's own dye load, not a colour-protection route; colour-DEPOSITING masks are excluded at G0 in any case); `lightness` blocked (weight_potential `high`). Step 4 `moisture` blocked at criterion 1 (PROPYLENE GLYCOL @5 is the only above-tail humectant-class species, against a required three). Step 5 `shine`: criterion 1 FAILS on the R4b lipid above the tail; criteria 2 and 3 are not reached. Step 6 `smoothing`: a distinct silicone route above the tail, materially beyond the ordinary mask base → selected.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `smoothing`: §9.5.2 step 6 — dry surface control is the clearest practical differentiator and the architecture extends materially beyond the ordinary mask base through AMODIMETHICONE @6.

`shine` does not apply — the substantive change from v0.1, and it fails on the FORMULA leg, not the claim leg. §9.5.4 criterion 1 is a conjunct: an alignment-oriented route AND a comparatively low lipid load AND no R4b heavy lipid above the tail. The last conjunct fails. §9.5.1's hard rule is then decisive: exact-product positioning may break a genuinely dual_supported tie but may never lower a candidate's own threshold or substitute for a corroboration leg the focus value requires in its own right. Gloss/Laminierung positioning is therefore recorded and creates nothing.

`shine` as a SECONDARY is also refused, for the same reason: criterion 1 is the route's own threshold and it failed, so there is no route to place in a slot. A slot spent on shine here would additionally be the free add-on of the smoothing film that §6 rule 2 and D2 forbid.
`general` does not apply: a candidate cleared at step 6.

There is NO lamination property and no `lamination` focus value (charter F4, D2, evidence §7). Gloss identity would have been carried entirely by `shine`; with `shine` failing its own threshold, it is carried by nothing, and that is the correct outcome for a formula whose acid sits at rank 29.

v0.1's blind lane selected `smoothing` and unblinding moved it to `shine` on criterion 3 — the single blind-to-final change across all 108 v0.1 fields. Under v0.2 the blind value stands and that change is withdrawn.
counterSignals: This is the most marker-sensitive call in the cohort, and v0.1's record said so in advance: 'if the marker were taken at Phenoxyethanol @13 instead of the colourant @7, Cocos Nucifera Oil @9 … would come above the tail … which would defeat criterion 1's low-lipid-load condition and collapse `shine` to `smoothing` or `general`.' R8 moved the marker (to @12, one rank earlier than that prediction) and the predicted collapse followed.

The result is uncomfortable in the other direction too: a product marketed entirely on gloss now carries no shine value anywhere in its profile. That is §9.5.4 working as written — the threshold is a formula threshold — but it is exactly the case §18 open question 6 asks about, and it is escalated rather than smoothed over.

`gloss_lamination_claim` review trigger fires, as it must for any Gloss/Glaze/Laminierung positioning: a human verifies that the shine threshold was tested independently and that the banned wording is absent.
limitations: Banned wording, absolute (evidence §7, §9.5.4, R6a): this record never says seals, versiegelt, closes the cuticle, laminates, lasting, permanent, or builds a protective layer that stays — notwithstanding that the product's own pack uses two of those words. Permitted and used: temporary optical/surface emphasis, comparative surface-control potential.
Glycolic acid temporarily plasticises the fibre (a measured decrease in Young's modulus) and does not seal, bond, or produce lasting change; its skin-exfoliation evidence is not imported.

adjudicationPoints.title: R8's colourant patch moves the marker, and one coconut oil at rank 9 then moves three fields — ESCALATION, largest unpredicted effect in the run
adjudicationPoints.body: The ruling ledger records R8 as 'no value moves'. On this product it moves three. Removing colourants from marker eligibility pushes tail_index from CI 17200 @7 to HYDROXYCITRONELLAL @12, which brings COCOS NUCIFERA OIL @9 into the credited segment. §5's R4b enumeration names Cocos Nucifera Oil among the heavy triglycerides, so: (1) §9.2's `high` anchor acquires its required heavy-lipid core and, with CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2 as the dense-base completer, `weight_potential` moves moderate → high; (2) §9.5.4 criterion 1 requires an optical architecture with no R4b heavy lipid above the tail, so the `shine` threshold fails and `primary_focus` moves shine → smoothing, withdrawing the cohort's only blind-to-final change; (3) `hair_thickness_fit` echoes to {normal, coarse}, dropping `fine`. The v0.1 record predicted this cascade in its own counter-signals, one rank off ('if the marker were taken at Phenoxyethanol @13 … Cocos Nucifera Oil @9 would come above the tail … which would defeat criterion 1'). So the derivation is not a surprise reading; it is the documented alternative becoming the rule. What needs a human: a five-minute gloss treatment now carries the category's richest weight prior on a single mid-list plant oil, and a product sold entirely on gloss carries no shine value anywhere in its profile. Both are the standard applied as written. The candidate levers, none of which this lane may pull, are (a) whether coconut oil at rank 9 of thirty is an R4b heavy lipid or a mid-band token — the lexicon's family-3 heavy band does not name it, while the standard's §5 does, and reconciling the two files is an open item; (b) whether §9.5.4 criterion 1's lipid condition should read the lipid's rank or merely its presence.
